title: Control plane: approval workflow endpoints for model changelog (draft → in_review → published) + RBAC checks
author: Jada Williams
description: Summary: Adds first-pass approval workflow primitives to the control plane for customer-visible model changelog entries. This introduces explicit state transitions (draft → in_review → published) with RBAC enforcement and optimistic concurrency. Motivation: Enterprise customers are asking for auditable, gated publication of model change notes; we also need a consistent internal workflow before docs/Console surfaces go live. This PR focuses on API and authorization only; generator integration + audit event enrichment are handled in follow-up PRs. API changes: - New resource: changelog entries with lifecycle state. - Endpoints (internal): POST /v1/model-changelog/entries (create draft), GET /v1/model-changelog/entries/{entry_id}, GET /v1/model-changelog/entries?model_id=&version_id=&state=&limit=&cursor=, POST /v1/model-changelog/entries/{entry_id}:submit (draft → in_review), POST /v1/model-changelog/entries/{entry_id}:publish (in_review → published), POST /v1/model-changelog/entries/{entry_id}:request_changes (in_review → draft, with required reviewer_note). - Adds If-Match style precondition via updated_at + revision integer (409 on conflict) to avoid overwriting reviewer edits. RBAC: - Introduces two explicit permissions: model_changelog:edit (create/update draft, submit for review, request changes) and model_changelog:publish (publish). - Adds a separate check for publication requiring both permission AND membership in Release Notes Approvers group (config-backed allowlist) to support interim enterprise expectations. - Non-admin users cannot publish their own entries unless they are in the approvers allowlist (prevents “self-approve” by default). Data model: - Adds fields: state, created_by, last_updated_by, submitted_at, submitted_by, reviewed_at, reviewed_by, published_at, published_by, reviewer_note. - Stores immutable snapshot of customer-visible content at publish time (title/summary/body + links) to prevent post-publish mutation; edits after publish are blocked (returns 400) until supersede flow lands. Validation: - submit requires non-empty customer_safe_summary and required compatibility section. - publish requires (a) state=in_review, (b) no unresolved redaction violations from template lint, (c) deprecation fields (if present) must include sunset_date. Tests: - Unit tests for state machine transitions and RBAC. - API tests for 403/409/422 responses and cursor pagination. Notes / follow-ups: - Audit log emission for state transitions will be expanded in PR-18821 (this PR adds basic structured logging only). - “Supersede/rollback” for published entries is intentionally not included here (tracked separately). - Console UI wiring will use these endpoints via the Console backend feature flag.
commits: api: add changelog entry lifecycle state + revision field
authz: add model_changelog:edit and model_changelog:publish permissions
openapi: document new endpoints + error shapes
conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can we make sure the transition endpoints are idempotent? E.g., publishing twice shouldn’t create two published artifacts. Also, what’s the canonical conflict signal for concurrent edits?

Jada Williams (author): Good call. Added: publish is idempotent if state==published (returns 200 with current resource). For concurrency we now use revision++ on write and return 409 conflict when revision mismatches; tests added in concurrency_test.go. Submit/request_changes remain strict (422 if wrong state) to avoid hiding misuse from callers.

Jordan Lee (review): RBAC looks right, but the “approvers allowlist” is a second authorization mechanism. Please document why we need it and ensure it’s config-driven + audited. Also, block self-approval by default.

Jada Williams (author): Updated description + inline comments: allowlist is interim until we fully align with centralized approval policies; it’s config-backed and only evaluated for publish. Implemented self-approval block unless caller is in allowlist AND has model_changelog:publish (so being in allowlist alone is not sufficient).
Connor O'Brien (review): Please confirm how this behaves during release freezes. Can release eng still publish urgent corrections? We need an emergency path that is explicit.

Jada Williams (author): For now: release eng users are included in release_notes_approvers.yaml. Emergency path will be a separate endpoint/flag with stricter auditing (tracked in PM-803 comments). Added a note to OpenAPI description that publish requires approver membership.
Marissa Cole (review): Can we enforce a minimum structure for customer-facing notes at submit time (compatibility, impact)? We don’t want reviewers chasing missing sections.

Jada Williams (author): Added validation at submit: requires customer_safe_summary and at least one compatibility note block; publish still re-validates plus checks deprecation constraints. Docs style lint is handled in generator PR, but this prevents empty shells from entering review.
Chloe Martin (final): Looks good after the idempotency + conflict additions. Approving.
